title.value: Optogenetic activation of parvalbumin and somatostatin interneurons selectively restores theta-nested gamma oscillations and oscillation-induced spike timing-dependent long-term potentiation impaired by amyloid β oligomers
title.justification: This is the title of the paper, as mentioned at the beginning of the document under the header 'RESEARCH ARTICLE'.
title.quote: Optogenetic activation of parvalbumin and somatostatin interneurons selectively restores theta-nested gamma oscillations and oscillation-induced spike timing-dependent long-term potentiation impaired by amyloid β oligomers

analysis.description: The paper focuses on how amyloid β 1–42 oligomers affect hippocampal theta-nested gamma oscillations and long-term potentiation in the context of Alzheimer's disease. It explores the role of parvalbumin (PV) and somatostatin (SST) interneurons in these processes and investigates the restoration of function through optogenetic activation.

type.justification: The paper presents experimental results involving optogenetic manipulations and computational modeling, which are empirical methods to study the impact of amyloid β on neuron circuits and potential restoration strategies.
type.quote: Through optogenetic manipulation of PV and SST interneurons and computational modeling of the hippocampal neural circuits, we dissected the contributions of PV and SST interneuron circuit dysfunctions on AβO 1–42 -induced impairments of hippocampal theta-nested gamma oscillations and oscillation-induced LTP.

name.justification: The paper investigates the neural circuits involving parvalbumin and somatostatin interneurons, aiming to understand their dysfunction in conditions like Alzheimer's disease.
name.quote: Parvalbumin-positive (PV) and somatostatin-positive (SST) interneurons are critically involved in theta-nested gamma oscillogenesis and LTP induction.

name.justification: The study specifically investigates dysfunctions and therapeutic targets relevant to Alzheimer's disease.
name.quote: Our results reveal that AβO 1–42 causes synapse-specific dysfunctions in PV and SST interneurons and that optogenetic modulations of these interneurons present potential therapeutic targets for restoring hippocampal network oscillations and synaptic plasticity impairments in Alzheimer’s disease.

name.justification: The paper describes the use of computational modeling to simulate the interactions between different types of neurons within the hippocampus.
name.quote: Finally, computational modeling of hippocampal neural circuits including CA1 PC, PV, and SST interneurons confirmed the experimental observations and further revealed distinct functional roles of PV and SST interneurons in theta-nested gamma oscillations and tLTP induction.

is_contributed.justification: The computational model was developed as part of the study to aid in understanding neuron interactions in the hippocampus affected by AβO 1–42.
is_contributed.quote: Finally, computational modeling of hippocampal neural circuits including CA1 PC, PV, and SST interneurons confirmed the experimental observations and further revealed distinct functional roles of PV and SST interneurons in theta-nested gamma oscillations and tLTP induction.
